speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, we have had to curtail and change many aspects of life that we are used to – school and work, but also family life and daily routines.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many of us have had to adjust our plans or put them on hold.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have had to accept greater uncertainty in our lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During the circuit breaker period, 2,723 couples were originally scheduled to have their solemnisations between 7 April and 1 June this year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, as marriage solemnisations must currently be conducted in person, many have had to postpone their solemnisations.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is not easy to cope with the uncertainty, especially for important life events, such as getting married and starting a family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While some couples may prefer to wait until it is safer to celebrate their big day in person with family and friends, others may not wish to wait any longer or may face extenuating circumstances that make postponement challenging.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I am, therefore, putting this Bill before the House.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will give eligible couples the option of making their statutory declarations and having their marriages solemnised via video link if they prefer not to wait to do so in person.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will now highlight the key provisions of this Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, clauses 2(1), 2(4), 3(1), 3(2), 3(3) and 4 will make it clear that certain key processes relating to marriage, which currently must be done in person, may be done via video link instead and will be equally valid under the law.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This applies to the verification of documents and the making of statutory declarations by the couple as well as the wali in the case of Muslim marriages, which currently must be done by the couple in the physical presence of a Commissioner for Oaths.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This also applies to the solemnisation of marriages.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While the temporary measures are in force, we will dispense with the requirement for the couple, witnesses, wali, as well as the licensed solemniser, Kadi or Naib Kadi to be physically present at the solemnisation venue.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we will put in place safeguards to ensure that only legitimate marriages are solemnised and registered through video link.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, there may be a small number of cases where the identities of the couple and relevant parties cannot be easily ascertained over video link, or where the case may involve a potential marriage of convenience, or parties possibly being coerced into marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Therefore, clauses 2(1) and 3(1) will give the Registry of Marriages and the Registry of Muslim Marriages the discretion to decide whether a video link can be used for verification and statutory declarations, as well as marriage solemnisations, for each marriage application.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This enables the Registrars to ensure that cases that require more careful scrutiny are still handled in person, when it is safe to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides this broad discretion, we will also put in place several key criteria.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, the Registrars must be satisfied that the overall administrative and technological facilities and arrangements are sufficient to ensure that the marriage is legitimate.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes ensuring that all parties involved have access to a computer or other smart devices that enable all parties to be adequately seen and heard and have their identities verified.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, consistent with the law today, the couple, their witnesses and, in the case of Muslim marriages, the wali, must all be physically present in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, couples presenting foreign-issued documents for verification will still need to do so physically.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This ensures greater scrutiny can be given to the veracity of the documents and the identities of the parties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a start, we are also prioritising video link processes to marriages involving at least one Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will add that while the Bill allows for solemnisations via video link to take place, it remains up to the solemniser and the couple to decide if they are comfortable and confident with doing so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Even with this option in place, we will seek to conduct solemnisations in person when it is safe to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, couples have to get married within three months from the date that they file their notice of marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, many couples have had to cancel their notices as they were unable to proceed with their wedding within the three-month period.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are also other logistical arrangements that need to be considered, such as the booking of wedding venues, photography, wedding gowns, wedding suits and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Couples do not need to re-apply for this extension.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope that the extension of the validity of the marriage licence will allow couples greater flexibility in planning their marriage solemnisation date as well as reduce the administrative burden.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The temporary measures effected by this Bill will apply and last until the COVID-19 pandemic improves.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If these temporary measures to allow the marriage process to be carried out via video link prove to be well received by couples and we are satisfied that there is no compromise to the integrity of the marriage process, we can consider extending this option beyond the COVID-19 period.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will require an amendment to the Women’s Charter and to AMLA.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: (In Mandarin):   As the COVID-19 pandemic evolved, we have had to put in place different measures to respond effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have had to change many aspects of life that we are used to.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many of us had to adjust our plans or put them on hold.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, marriage solemnisation must be conducted in person.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a result, many solemnisations have had to be postponed during the circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, the couples, their witnesses, and in the case of Muslim marriages, the wali, must be physically present in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, couples presenting foreign-issued documents for verifications will still need to do so physically.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This ensures that greater scrutiny can be given to the veracity of the documents and the identities of the parties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, the Registrars will still have the power to require any couple to go through the marriage processes physically instead of through video link.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This enables the Registrars to ensure that cases that require more careful scrutiny are still handled in person, when it is safe to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, in conclusion, it is vital during these trying times for us to ensure that Singaporeans can continue with key life milestones, with precautions and safeguards put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have to adapt to the current climate, and prepare ourselves for possible new norms in our social lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through process re-engineering, tapping on innovation and technology and making adjustments to the way we conduct our lives, it is possible for us to cope, adjust and adapt, even under the cloud of the global pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope that this Bill will give couples more options to plan their next step in life and reduce the disruption arising from COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We understand that this period has caused a lot of uncertainty and concern to couples who are planning to get married.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The teams at ROM and ROMM have been working hard to reach out to couples who have had their wedding plans affected, to work with them to postpone their weddings and work out alternative arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides thanking these couples for their understanding and patience during this period, I would also like to record my appreciation for the hard work of our frontline officers at both ROM and ROMM who are supporting and helping our couples.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Marriage is one of the most important milestones in life.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We need to take urgent steps to ensure that Singaporean couples can proceed with their marriage plans and be supported in their new family lives, despite the challenging circumstances.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: All over the world, marriage solemnisation, in all its different formats, has usually involved the couple, their families, friends, well-wishers and a solemniser gathering at a formal ceremony.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I used to be a solemniser when I was working at the People Association’s Family Life Unit.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many couples whom I solemnised sought advice and I even provided counselling to some.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They appreciated this as I shared my own marriage and family life experience and they found it very helpful.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Couples who have attended marriage preparation programmes prior to their marriage registration would have learnt about couple communications and problem-solving skills.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For those who have not, the solemnisation process presents an opportunity for the solemnisers to offer such important advice and share valuable personal experiences in person.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that with solemnisation conducted via video links, this important part of the process shall be required to remain incorporated as well.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   Many couples whom I solemnised, sought advice from me and I even provided some counselling to some of them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They appreciated this as I shared my own marriage experiences and they found it helpful.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Couples who have attended marriage preparation programmes prior to their marriage registration would have learnt about couple communications and problem-solving skills.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For those who have not attended such programmes, the solemnization process presents an opportunity for the solemnizers to offer such important advice and share valuable personal experiences.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that with solemnization conducted through video links, this important part of the process shall be required to remain incorporated as well.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): For couples who are interested, solemnisers are an important connector who can point them to resources where they can get further support in their new married lives, including marriage preparation programmes which are also available to married couples.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is never too late to learn more about communication, conflict-resolution, household financial management skills, family planning and health screening, how to relate to in-laws, and more.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Solemnisers can also promote customised service for the unique circumstance of each couple and point them to the relevant Government agency or Ministry should they require further support for this new stage of their lives.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: All these advisories and support are crucial for laying a robust foundation for strong marriages and families in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This could help expedite application and registration processes and reduce red tape.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I look forward to the Minister’s clarifications and conclude with my support for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Marriage celebrations and ceremonies are often rich in tradition, heritage and cultural significance.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But even where such celebrations are not possible during this period of time, at least that part of the marriage that confers a legal status can still be carried out.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is because there is a legal significance to marriage, bringing along rights, responsibilities and some privileges.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For instance, the ability to obtain public housing, certain tax reliefs, adoption of children, immigration and so on.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Because of the importance family life and the family unit has to Singapore, it is good that we can have such a Bill to allow marriages to continue taking place even during this time.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Many couples look forward to celebrating their what is often once-in-a-life-time ceremony.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While the couple may not be familiar with the solemniser, their witnesses are often their parents, family members or closest friends.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A marriage is a significant milestone for families, and the couple may not just desire but also feel it only right and fair that families and parents from both sides be physically present to witness the solemnisation of their marriage.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: After all, marriage is the legal union between a man and a woman, husband and wife.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It reflects the foundational family unit in our society.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Allowing for cancellation of a notice of marriage is different from what is currently provided for in the law.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Currently, when a notice of marriage is filed, the parties are not able to cancel it but have to wait for the three months to lapse if they no longer wish to proceed further towards solemnisation of their marriage.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, my first clarification is: are we going to allow parties to cancel their notice of marriage?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Following on from this, if we are allowing them to cancel their notice of marriage, what is the legal mechanism for it and under what circumstances can they cancel it?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Currently, the Women's Charter does not provide for the cancellation of a notice of marriage.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This position is also reflected in the Registry of Marriage's Frequently Asked Questions.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Since the law, as it currently stands, does not provide for cancellation, the other possible place for such a power would be this Bill that we are debating today.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While it provides that the Registrar can impose conditions relating to the use of remote communication technology under clause 2(1)(c), it does not convey rule-making power to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, to repeat my second clarification, if we are allowing parties to cancel their notice of marriage, what is the legal mechanism for it and under what circumstances can they do so?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My third clarification, is, if we are going to change the law to allow parties to cancel their notice of marriage, why are we making such a change?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Allowing it to be cancelled is a material change to the effect of such a notice.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Being locked in for a period of three months without being able to cancel a notice is different from having a notice last for 12 months and being able to cancel it at any point in time.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The effect this has on parties deciding to file a notice of marriage would be different.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Filing a notice of marriage is the first step towards a marriage that is recognised by civil law.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Marriage is a lifetime commitment and, according to Article 94(2) of the Women's Charter, newly-wedded couples are not able to obtain a divorce within the first three years unless there is exceptional circumstance.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Since marriage is such a long-term commitment, it would seem, at least at first glance, a little strange to change the law to allow a notice of marriage to be entered into less seriously, as parties are able to cancel it at any time instead of being locked-in for a certain period of time until the notice lapses.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, if we are going to change the law such that parties may cancel their notice of marriage, why are we making such a change?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is good that marriages can continue to happen during the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Notwithstanding the clarifications I seek, I support this Bill.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The current COVID-19 situation has disrupted our lives on many fronts – work, school, businesses, our social lives and significant life events, be it birthdays, funerals or weddings.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, the verification of documents, making of statutory declarations and solemnisation of the marriage have to be done in person.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I support the flexibility accorded for marriages to take place during this period of restrictions in movement and interactions, I do have several concerns and clarifications that I hope can be addressed.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One, for civil marriages, will our Licensed Solemnisers be provided with some form of training to help them carry out their duties through virtual or online means?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This training could be in the form of online courses and videos that they ought to undergo and complete prior to solemnising a civil marriage through virtual means henceforth.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How many marriages have had to be postponed and were there appeals for some of these marriages to be solemnised as soon as possible?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Three, Muslim marriages are also religious rites and, traditionally, this has involved many aspects and significant individuals in the bride and groom's life, such as requiring the Kadi or Naib Kadi, the marrying couple, the Wali and required witnesses to gather.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How will these temporary measures account for the religious aspects of a marriage?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will virtual marriages be regarded as religiously married for Muslims?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Four, for Muslim marriages that require the involvement of many more individuals, again, the Kadi or Naib Kadi, the Wali and the required witnesses, how do we ensure that all of them can be virtually present with the required technological tools and Internet connection, for instance?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are there plans to provide the Kadi or Naib Kadi and required witnesses centrally from the Syariah Court, for example, to ensure that they are equipped with the required technological tools and Internet connection in order for the Muslim marriage to be solemnised virtually?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I look forward to the response from the Minister on my questions above.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For these couples, the disruption has been disappointing as marriage is a major life event, and we thank them for their civic-mindedness in putting the collective safety of Singaporeans first.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To answer Dr Intan's question, ROMM will train and assist Kadis and Naib Kadis to ensure they are able to use remote technology during this period.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As part of the approval process, the Registrar must check that the parties have the necessary technical facilities where they reside.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Couples who are not eligible for these remote processes may still apply for in-person solemnisations when it is safe to do so.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Regardless, I would like to stress that even for those who qualify for video link solemnisations, physical receptions and celebratory gatherings must continue to be postponed until it is safe.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Throughout our fight against COVID-19, Singaporeans have had to change our usual ways and adopt new social norms.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In our community, we adapted the way we salam to minimise human contact and avoided congregational prayers in the mosques during this period.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The adaptations we have made to our social and religious norms do not make us any less of a Muslim and, similarly, adaptations to the way we conduct Muslim marriage processes do not mean that we do not observe religious imperatives.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):   Dr Intan also asked whether these temporary measures take into account the conditions for marriage from a religious standpoint and whether video link marriages be will regarded as valid from a religious perspective.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The spirit of the Administration of Muslim Law Act or AMLA is to facilitate the religious way of life for Muslims in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: ROMM will also provide guidelines to the Kadis and Naib Kadis on ways to conduct solemnizations through video links.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am also heartened that our asatizah are taking progressive and practical steps to fulfil the needs of Muslims in Singapore during these challenging times.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is in line with developments in Muslim communities around the world.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For instance, in India, Indonesia, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Malaysia, Muslim couples have already embraced the use of remote technology for solemnizations.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has posed an unprecedented challenge to us all.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But together, we will do our best to minimise disruptions to the lives of Singaporeans, without compromising our collective safety.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, I support this Bill.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: About 1,100 civil marriages and close to 200 Muslim marriages have so far been postponed, and most of the remaining would also have to be postponed if there is no video link option.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Dr Intan asked whether Licensed Solemnisers will be provided with training to solemnise civil marriages via video link.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Indeed, as this is a new process, it is important to make sure that solemnisers are comfortable and confident performing solemnisations over video link and to ensure that the process is done properly so that the solemnisation is valid.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ROM will be providing a set of guidelines and a basic training video to all Licensed Solemnisers called upon to solemnise marriages through video link.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They can also approach ROM if they have any queries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked whether solemnisers could tap on the video link to offer marital advice to couples as they embark on their marriage journey.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I agree that this is an important role that solemnisers play beyond the process of solemnising the marriage itself.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Like the current in-person process, solemnisers can certainly share marital advice during the solemnisation process through video link.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If they feel that more time is needed, the couples and solemnisers are able to contact one another remotely, before or after the solemnisation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Christopher de Souza commented on the need to regularly review the COVID-19 situation and whether there is still a need to allow for marriage solemnisation through video link.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Those who can wait and prefer to solemnise their marriage in person can still do so when it is safe to do so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also review the need for these temporary measures regularly, taking into account the COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Christopher de Souza also asked whether the new Bill allows parties to cancel their notice of marriage, the rationale for doing so and under what circumstances notices of marriage can be cancelled.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I fully agree with him that filing a notice of marriage holds particular meaning by signifying that the couple has made a considered decision to enter into marriage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under normal circumstances, when a couple files a notice of marriage, they need to wait till after the three-month notice period lapses if they wish to reschedule their marriage to a much later date beyond the three-month period.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: However, due to the fluidity and uncertainty posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, we would like to provide couples with more flexibility to plan their marriages.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With a longer validity period, couples need not repeatedly file notices of marriage and wait for the mandatory 21-day period for each notice to be over before they proceed to get married.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Each application for cancellation will be reviewed by the Registrar before the Registrar cancels the notice.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have said earlier, it is important during these challenging times that we ensure that Singaporeans can continue with their lives, especially for key life events like marriage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This Bill ensures that couples can continue to get married and embark on a new stage in life together by tapping on technology and keeping to the necessary precautions.
